seo_description: Prepare for the FCP Part 1, the CMSA basic sciences paper for internal medicine, with Passmed’s physician-reviewed SBA question bank and study modes.
seo_keywords: FCP Part 1, CMSA fellowship, internal medicine exam, College of Physicians SA, FCP question bank
content:
FCP Part 1 Overview

The FCP (Fellowship of the College of Physicians of South Africa) is the postgraduate examination required for specialist registration in Internal Medicine in South Africa. The examination consists of two parts: Part 1 covers basic sciences, and Part 2 covers the principles and practice of medicine, applied basic science, diagnosis, and treatment.

Part 1 is valid for six years; Part 2 must be passed within four years of completing registrar training time.

FCP Part 1 Details

FormatComputer-based MCQ - best of 5
Structure1 paper
Duration3 hours
Questions150 SBA questions
Pass markCohen's method of standard setting
ValidityPass valid for 6 years
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • No prior exam requirements to sit FCP Part 1.
  • Open to candidates with a post-internship medical qualification registered with the HPCSA.

seo_description: Prepare for the FCP Part 2 clinical medicine examination with Passmed’s physician-reviewed SBA question bank, timed and tutor modes, and analytics.
seo_keywords: FCP Part 2, CMSA fellowship, internal medicine exam, College of Physicians SA, FCP question bank
content:
FCP Part 2 Overview

FCP Part 2 builds on Part 1 and assesses the principles and practice of medicine, applied basic science, diagnosis, and treatment. Part 2 consists of three sections: MCQ exam, Objective Test, and Clinical exam.

Candidates who have completed both Part I and Part 2 of the MRCP(UK) may be exempt from FCP Part I. Part 2 must be passed within four years of completing registrar training time.

FCP Part 2 Details

FormatMCQ - best of 4
Structure2 papers (75 questions each)
Duration3 hours
Questions150 questions (MCQ paper)
Other componentsObjective test + Clinical exam
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Post-community service medical qualification registered with the HPCSA.
  • Completed 30 months full-time post-internship training as a medical registrar or clinical assistant.
  • Passed FCP Part 1 (or exempt via full MRCP(UK)).
  • Supervisors' approval of the candidate's portfolio.

FCS Primary Overview

The Primary is the entry-level examination covering the basic sciences foundation required for surgical training - anatomy, physiology, and pathology.

Paper 1Anatomy MCQs - 120 questions
Paper 2Physiology / Pathology / Miscellaneous - 120 questions
Duration3 hours each paper
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Post-internship qualification registered with the HPCSA or any other medical council.
  • Successfully completed the 3-day Basic Surgical Skills course or the Basic and Essential Surgical Skills Training (BESST) course.

content:
FCOG Primary Overview

As of 2024, the FCOG(SA) consists of three examinations: Primary, Intermediate, and Final. The Primary examination is designed to assess candidates' understanding of fundamental scientific principles related to obstetrics and gynaecology.

The exam covers anatomy, embryology, physiology, endocrinology, immunology, cell biology, pathology, microbiology/virology, pharmacology, pathophysiology, statistics, and bioethics.

FCOG Primary Details

FormatComputer-based SBA MCQ
Structure1 paper
Duration3 hours
Questions150 Single Best Answer questions
MarkingStandard setting; no negative marking
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Hold a recognized medical degree with a post-internship qualification to practise medicine.
  • Be registered with the HPCSA or an equivalent regulatory authority.

content:
FCOG Intermediate Overview

The FCOG(SA) Intermediate is the second of the three FCOG examinations. It is a computer-based test (CBT) covering clinical obstetrics and gynaecology as well as relevant basic medical sciences.

Candidates are permitted a maximum of six attempts to pass the Intermediate exam. The exam is machine-marked; 1 mark for each correct answer, 0 for incorrect; no negative marking. The pass mark is determined using standard setting methods.

FCOG Intermediate Details

FormatComputer-based SBA MCQ
Structure1 paper
Duration3 hours
Questions150 SBA questions
AttemptsUp to 6 attempts permitted
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Passed the FCOG(SA) Primary, or the Part 1 Fellowship of a recognised college with reciprocal agreements.
  • Completed a minimum of 12 months in a registrar training post in an accredited department approved by the CMSA.

content:
FCEM Part 2 Overview

FCEM Part 2 assesses the principles and practice of emergency medicine, including investigations, diagnosis, treatment, and disposal. The exam consists of eight separate components - three written and five oral/practical.

To pass, candidates must achieve 45% or more for all components and an overall average of 50%. Candidates must also pass at least half the questions in each written paper and at least four of the five practical components.

FCEM Part 2 Details

Written - case papers2 papers, 6 questions each, 3 hours
Written - MCQ100 questions over 2 hours
Practical - OSPE15 stations, 5 minutes each
Practical - clinical cases2 short cases (15-20 min)
Practical - simulations2 emergency simulations (12-20 min)
Practical - orals2 x 30-minute orals
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • 36 months in a numbered registrar training post.
  • Critical Performance Portfolio.

content:
FC Psych Part 1 Overview

The FC Psych (Fellowship of the College of Psychiatrists of South Africa) comprises Part 1 and Part 2. Part 2 must be passed within six years of passing Part 1, and within 36 months of completing registrar training time (defined as 48 months).

The Part 1 is a written examination administered electronically on the Speedwell System - candidates must write both papers in one sitting and pass both. No carry-over is possible.

FCPsych Part 1 Details

FormatElectronic written (Speedwell)
Structure2 papers
Paper 1Clinical Neurosciences - 100 questions
Paper 2Intro to Psychiatry + Psychology/Behavioural Sciences - 100 questions
Duration3 hours per paper
Question typesSBAs, MCQs, EMQs, very short answer
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Hold a post-internship qualification with full HPCSA registration.
  • Completed at least 1 year of community service post-internship.

content:
FCMFOS Primary Overview

The FCMFOS(SA) examination consists of three parts: Primary (Part 1A), Intermediate (Part 1B), and Final (Part 2). The examination is administered by the Colleges of Medicine of South Africa (CMSA) and follows a structured assessment format to ensure competency in maxillofacial and oral surgery.

A minimum pass mark of 50% is required in each subject. Candidates who fail one subject but score at least 40% may reattempt the failed subject in the next two consecutive sittings.

FCMFOS Primary Details

FormatWritten papers (SBA-MCQ + short essay)
Paper 1Anatomy & Embryology - 100-150 SBA-MCQs (3 hours)
Paper 2Physiology - MCQs + short essays (150 marks, 3 hours)
Paper 3Principles of Pathology including Microbiology - 150 marks (3 hours)
Pass mark50% in each subject
Official source: cmsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Hold a dental or medical qualification registerable with the HPCSA.
  • Submit an application through the CMSA website with verified credentials.

content:
HPCSA Board Exam Overview

The HPCSA Board Examination is aligned with the Health Professions Act No. 56 of 1974 and assesses clinical, ethical, and medico-legal knowledge for foreign-qualified medical practitioners seeking registration to practise medicine in South Africa.

It comprises a written examination (MCQ) and a practical examination (OSCE/OSPE). A minimum score of 50% is required in each component to qualify for the practical exam.

HPCSA Board Exam Details

Written formatMCQ - no negative marking
Written clinical75 questions (clinical knowledge)
Written ethics25 questions (ethical & medico-legal)
Written duration3 hours
PracticalOSCE/OSPE - minimum 13 stations
LocationsPretoria, Durban, Cape Town (written)
Official source: hpcsa.co.za ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Completed application form (Form 12).
  • Certified copies of medical qualification and translations.
  • Proof of English proficiency (IELTS Band 6 minimum).
  • Verification of credentials via ECFMG.
  • CV, Certificate of Good Standing, valid passport or ID.
  • Documentary proof of internship and clinical experience.
  • Endorsement letter from the Directorate Workforce Management (DWM), Department of Health.
